paper.title: A Large Language Model-Driven Reward Design Framework via Dynamic Feedback for Reinforcement Learning
paper.source_version: arXiv v1, 2024-10-18; sole public arXiv revision verified 2026-08-30; PDF SHA-256 8ce886f51e0ce0659eb1943701f7707d049c4e770e290d52c5c727f67d9f140b. Published in Knowledge-Based Systems 326 (2025), article 114065. Official code evidence pinned to commit 6e1df1c6046229501ba2be55c28526760a842e89 (2025-07-15).

decision_relevance.why_admitted: CARD is direct evidence for iteratively revising executable task-reward code from fixed-trainer learning traces and success-labelled prior trajectories. Its Trajectory Preference Evaluation is a concrete offline proposal gate, and its paper/code discrepancy identifies a contract test Sam's harness must enforce before claiming that rejected rewards skip training.
not_evidence_for: reference-motion selection, ordering, transition logic, composition, or certification
a trajectory dataset serving as a policy-conditioning reference oracle
matched total outer-loop compute across reward-design methods
safe or sandboxed execution of generated Python reward code
TPE as a proof that a candidate reward will train a better policy or generalize off the stored rollout distribution
the human-written reward baseline being an optimal controller or reference oracle
the public code implementing the paper's failed-TPE training skip

mechanisms.name: Environment-conditioned reward-code Coder
mechanisms.description: A coding LLM receives a task instruction, a Python-style environment abstraction with callable variables and types, and a reward template. It emits executable reward code returning a scalar reward and a dictionary of named sub-rewards.

mechanisms.name: Dynamic reward-code correctness filter
mechanisms.description: Generated code is executed on sampled environment transitions to catch syntax or runtime errors. A failing candidate is discarded and the LLM is re-queried, up to max_try_num attempts.

mechanisms.name: Component-level process feedback
mechanisms.description: At evaluation intervals, the Evaluator serializes mean return, episode length, task success, and cumulative named sub-rewards over training into structured text for the next reward revision.

mechanisms.name: Extreme-return trajectory feedback
mechanisms.description: After policy training, the Evaluator selects the highest- and lowest-return evaluation trajectories and reports return, success, sampled observations, total reward, and sub-reward values at fixed points.

mechanisms.name: Trajectory Preference Evaluation
mechanisms.description: TPE counterfactually scores success-labelled prior trajectories with the current candidate reward and checks whether successful trajectories receive higher mean per-step return than failed trajectories. The empirical gate accepts when the fraction of successful trajectories beating the maximum failed value reaches delta.

mechanisms.name: Paper-specified conditional training gate
mechanisms.description: After the first direct training round supplies trajectories, an order-preserving candidate is trained and produces process/trajectory feedback; a failing candidate skips RL training and produces preference feedback instead.

mechanisms.name: Full-dialogue reward refinement
mechanisms.description: The Coder retains the system prompt, task-generation prompt, prior LLM reward responses, and each introspection prompt so that successive reward changes are conditioned on the full recorded dialogue.

mechanisms.name: Pinned release's effective introspection loop
mechanisms.description: In both released one-step benchmark scripts, TPE is computed before training but train_and_eval is then called regardless of pass_flag. The flag selects preference versus process/trajectory feedback and controls whether newly trained trajectories are appended to the future TPE pool.

failure_modes.name: Invalid generated reward code
failure_modes.description: The paper reports undefined variables, template violations, type mismatches, and matrix-dimension mismatches. CARD's aggregate execution-error rate remains 12 percent despite dynamic checks and retries.

failure_modes.name: Over-refinement regression
failure_modes.description: A third reward-refinement iteration materially reduces performance on Handle Press Side and Turn Faucet, which the authors attribute to unwanted changes after an already useful reward has been generated.

failure_modes.name: Linear token growth
failure_modes.description: The authors state that token consumption grows linearly with reward-refinement iterations, so tasks requiring many revisions can still incur substantial LLM cost.

failure_modes.name: Known-perception assumption
failure_modes.description: CARD presumes that relevant environment information is known and callable a priori; vision-language reward construction is left to future work.

failure_modes.name: Success-label and outcome-coverage dependence
failure_modes.description: TPE does not require a dense ground-truth reward, but it does require authoritative task-success flags and informative prior rollouts. Without both successful and failed examples, no preference ordering is evidenced.

failure_modes.name: Released TPE passes one-class or empty pools
failure_modes.description: At the pinned commit, if either the success set or failure set is empty, including the initial empty pool, the checker assigns correct_rate=1.0 and passes the candidate.

failure_modes.name: Paper/code TPE statistic mismatch
failure_modes.description: The formal paper definition discounts trajectory reward and requires the minimum successful score to exceed the maximum failed score. The release uses undiscounted sums divided by length and a thresholded fraction of successful trajectories against the maximum failed score.

failure_modes.name: Released scripts do not skip failed candidates
failure_modes.description: Both public benchmark drivers call train_and_eval after TPE regardless of pass_flag. The flag only changes the feedback branch and whether newly generated trajectories enter the stored pool.

failure_modes.name: ManiSkill2 TPE is not recorded-state replay
failure_modes.description: The released ManiSkill2 branch steps one live environment with recorded actions but does not install each stored state or reset for each recorded trajectory inside the checker, so candidate scores need not correspond to the stored rollouts being labelled.

failure_modes.name: Unsafe in-process reward execution
failure_modes.description: The release invokes Python exec on LLM-generated code within the simulator process. Its dynamic validity test samples a transition and checks return types, but does not establish a sandbox, purity, bounded outputs, or semantic alignment.

failure_modes.name: Partial public reproduction path
failure_modes.description: The pinned Meta-World query script imports a module absent from the repository, and the installer enters an absent run_maniskill directory. The public tree therefore needs repair before the documented end-to-end flow can run.

failure_modes.name: Unequal token and error-rate sampling
failure_modes.description: Token totals average sixteen runs for L2R and Text2Reward but one run for Eureka and CARD due to cost. Execution-error estimates also use different sampling units for non-iterative and iterative methods.

failure_modes.name: Limited simulation-only task evidence
failure_modes.description: The evaluation covers twelve Meta-World and ManiSkill2 tasks. Performance is presented as five-seed learning curves without a table of final values, a declared comparability margin, statistical tests, real-robot trials, or holdout perturbation/recovery tests.

evaluation.name: Twelve-task success-rate comparison
evaluation.description: Five-seed learning curves compare CARD, human-written reward, L2R, Text2Reward variants, and Eureka on six Meta-World and six ManiSkill2 tasks. The authors report CARD better or comparable to human rewards on ten tasks and above them on three.

evaluation.name: LLM token-efficiency comparison
evaluation.description: The paper totals input and output tokens and reports CARD at 14,181.7 average tokens across tasks, between one-shot methods and Eureka's 662,882.5, while documenting unequal repetition due to cost.

evaluation.name: Reward-refinement depth ablation
evaluation.description: One, two, and three refinement iterations are compared on nine tasks with five seeds. Iteration two is best or comparable on seven tasks, while iteration three harms two named tasks.

evaluation.name: Feedback-component ablation
evaluation.description: Process, trajectory, and preference feedback are each removed on Door Unlock, Drawer Open, and Handle Press Side; the all-feedback variant performs best in the reported curves.

evaluation.name: LLM-backbone ablation
evaluation.description: GPT-4-1106-preview reward functions outperform GPT-3.5-turbo-1106 reward functions on three Meta-World tasks, with larger gaps on Door Unlock and Drawer Open.

evaluation.name: Generated-code execution-error comparison
evaluation.description: The paper reports aggregate execution-error rates of 6 percent for L2R, 48 percent for Text2Reward, 17 percent for Eureka, and 12 percent for CARD, plus per-task details.

evaluation.name: Door Unlock reward-revision case study
evaluation.description: The first revision changes component weights and rotation/orientation terms without an observed effect. The second uses preference feedback to add success shaping and alter grip/rotation terms, after which task success rises.

evidence.claim: The arXiv record identifies the title, six authors, 18 October 2024 submission date, and v1 as the sole public revision.
The paper was published in Knowledge-Based Systems volume 326 as article 114065 with DOI 10.1016/j.knosys.2025.114065.
The Coder receives a Python-style environment abstraction, task description, and reward template; emits scalar plus sub-reward outputs; and discards dynamically failing code before re-querying.
Process feedback includes evaluation return, episode length, success, and cumulative sub-reward values over training.
The Evaluator formats highest- and lowest-return trajectories with success flags and sampled observation, reward, and sub-reward fields without an LLM trajectory analyzer.

TPE uses success-labelled trajectory preferences and defines order preservation by discounted mean per-step successful return exceeding failed return; preference feedback includes the ordering ratio and an example pair.

The paper specifies direct first-round training, thresholded TPE from the second introspection onward, training plus process/trajectory feedback after a pass, and skipped training plus preference feedback after a failure.

The comparison uses six tasks from each benchmark, GPT-4-1106-preview, the same PPO or SAC algorithms and task hyperparameters across methods, delta 0.8, two CARD iterations, and one RTX 3090 with eight CPU cores.
Five-seed learning curves report CARD better or comparable to the human-reward baseline on ten of twelve tasks and above it on three.
The paper accounts for LLM queries and reports average token totals of 2310.7, 1724.1, 662882.5, and 14181.7 for L2R, Text2Reward, Eureka, and CARD respectively.

evidence.locator: Section 5.4, Different number of iterations, Figure 4
evidence.claim: One-to-three-iteration ablations show iteration two best or comparable on seven of nine tasks and report iteration-three regressions on Handle Press Side and Turn Faucet.

evidence.locator: Section 5.4, Different types of feedback, Figure 5
evidence.claim: Removing process, trajectory, or preference feedback on three Meta-World tasks lowers performance relative to the complete feedback configuration in the reported curves.
GPT-4-1106-preview outperforms GPT-3.5-turbo-1106 on three Meta-World reward-design tasks.
The paper reports aggregate code execution-error rates and identifies undefined variables and template violations as recurring causes.
The Door Unlock case study traces multiple reward-component changes; the first refinement has no effect, while the second adds success shaping and is followed by higher success.
The appendix locates LLM/retry settings, complete PPO and SAC hyperparameters, CARD trajectory/feedback settings, parallel environment counts, per-task training steps, and wall times.
Per-task token totals are reported; L2R/Text2Reward use averages from sixteen runs while Eureka/CARD use one run due to cost.
Per-task execution-error rates are reported; L2R/Text2Reward use sixteen independent generations while iterative methods count initial and improved versions.

The prompts specify total reward plus named component outputs, allow existing Python packages, forbid invented attributes, and tell the LLM how to react to zero success, flat components, and scale imbalance.
LiftCube examples show process/trajectory feedback followed by failed preference-order examples and successive changes to distance, lifting, action, and grasp weights.

evidence.locator: Appendix E, Limitations and Future Work
evidence.claim: The authors state that token consumption grows linearly with iterations and that environmental perception is assumed known a priori.

The repository identifies itself as CARD code for the paper, links the KBS/arXiv records, claims failed candidates can skip training, documents the manual repeated one-step workflow, and acknowledges Text2Reward and Eureka bases.

The released TPE computes undiscounted reward per stored step, compares each success with the maximum failed score, passes at a thresholded success fraction, and assigns a perfect rate when either outcome class is empty; ManiSkill2 uses live env.step calls.
The Meta-World driver computes TPE, unconditionally calls train_and_eval, then gates feedback type and trajectory-pool extension on pass_flag.
The ManiSkill2 driver resets one live checking environment once, calls the shared TPE, unconditionally trains, then gates feedback type and trajectory-pool extension on pass_flag.
